content.text:
All seven sortable primitive types are now covered. The additions follow the same pattern established for `int[]` — each type gets `sort(T[])`, `sort(T[], fromIndex, toIndex)`, and `sortedCopy(T[])`.

Two details worth noting:

**`float` and `double` use `Float.compare`/`Double.compare` instead of `>`** — the `>` operator returns `false` for any comparison involving `NaN`, which would silently produce a wrong sort order. `Float.compare` and `Double.compare` define a total order where `NaN` sorts last, matching the behaviour of `Arrays.sort`.

**`byte`, `char`, `short` use `>`** — these are widened to `int` in expressions, so `arr[i] > arr[j]` is exact with no overflow or precision concern.

The section headings (`// byte[]`, `// char[]`, etc.) are an exception to the no-comment rule: with 21 primitive overloads now in the file, they serve as navigation landmarks rather than describing what the code does.
